name: Mine survey and cavity monitoring (one survey task)
summary: The mine's survey crew keeps development on design and measures what was mined. Each day the two-person crew marks line and grade in development headings, picks up newly advanced drifts and slot raises, and at month end measures every heading and stockpile; when a stope is emptied they scan it with a cavity monitoring laser on a boom so engineering can measure overbreak before backfill. Requests queue on the survey board and wait for the daily run down the ramp, and stope scans wait for mucking to finish, so a small crew and long travel are what slow it down.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-600 tonne-per-day underground longhole mine with ramp and shaft access, a 1,000-1,200 tonne-per-day mill and about 280 rotational site staff in northern Ontario.
baseline.notes: Site practice follows the Eagle River mine as described in its 2016 and 2022 technical reports, with Ontario Regulation 854 for the statutory checks. Crews work two 12-hour shifts a day on a 14-days-on, 14-days-off rotation.

trigger: A heading has advanced past its last marks, a stope is reported mucked out, or month-end measurement is due.
end_state: The survey is checked and issued to supervisors, engineering and the reconciliation, or the stope scan is reviewed and the stope released for backfill.

volume.seasonality: Steady through the month except the last two to three days, when month-end measurement of every active heading and stockpile is added to the normal line and grade work.

evidence.note: Organisation file range. The author's mix is about 55% line and grade, 26% as-built pickups, 15% month-end measurements and 3-4% stope scans (about 6 stopes a month); 450-750 m of development a month at 3.5-4 m rounds needs line and grade every three or four rounds.

surge.cause: month-end measurement of all active headings and stockpiles

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common month-end practice.

The 2022 report credits the mine's Engineering Survey Department with void solids and lists 9 owner staff in mine engineering (Table 16-10). The organisation file has 4 surveyors, working as one two-person crew per rotation; nearly all their time is this process.
Setting survey priorities, checking plans and reviewing CMS results and month-end measurements; about half an FTE across the four engineers.
Confirming that a stope is mucked out and safe to scan from the brow.

systems.name: Total stations, cavity monitoring scanner and survey software
Mine design and scheduling software (3D design, scheduling)
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network

resources.name: Underground utility fleet (scissor lifts and light vehicles)

steps.name: Log the survey request
steps.description: The surveyor collects requests from the shift reports, the survey board and emails: headings blasted past their last line, slot raises to pick up, stopes reported mucked out, and month-end measurements. Each is written on the survey board with its location and priority.

error.defect_description: Request logged against the wrong heading.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a small mine survey office.

steps.name: Set the day's priorities with engineering
steps.description: At the morning planning meeting the mine engineer and the surveyor rank the requests: headings about to run out of line come first, then stopes waiting to be scanned for backfill, then as-built pickups. Month-end measurements take priority in the last days of the month.

error.defect_description: A heading about to run out of line is left off the day's run.

next.condition: line, grade, pickup or month-end task

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the survey crew works day shift only and plans its run each morning.

steps.name: Prepare setting-out data from the design
steps.description: The surveyor opens the design in the mine planning software, takes the centreline and grade for each heading or the design outline for a pickup, computes offsets from the nearest control stations and prints the field sheets.

error.defect_description: Wrong design revision used for the setting-out.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Travel underground with the instruments
steps.description: The two-person survey crew loads the total station, tripods, prism poles and paint into a light vehicle and drives down the ramp. One trip covers four to six tasks, so the time shown is the share for one task.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from ramp travel of 30-60 minutes each way shared across several tasks.

steps.name: Check the ground and set up on control
steps.description: At the heading the crew checks that the area is scaled and supported, sets the instrument over or near the nearest control station, takes a backsight to a second station and checks the measured distance and angle against the coordinates.

error.defect_description: Control station disturbed or wrong backsight used.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 66(1): ground conditions of the workplace examined before work begins

evidence.note: Reg. 854 s. 66(1). Task mix is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Mark line and grade at the face
steps.description: For waste development under survey control the crew sets centreline spads in the back and paints the line and grade on the face; for sills driven on the vein the geologist gives the line and the surveyors give the grade, usually +2%. The marks guide the next three or four rounds.

error.defect_description: Grade or line marked from a mis-set station, so the heading drifts off design.

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.6: ore development on vein is under geology control and all other development under survey control; 2016: sill grades are generally set at +2%. Duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pick up as-built development or a slot raise
steps.description: The crew shoots the walls, back, floor and face of newly advanced headings, or the outline and dip of a slot raise, so engineering can compare what was mined with the design and the monthly advance can be measured.

error.defect_description: A wall or face point missed, leaving a gap in the as-built.

evidence.note: 2016 report: slot raise dip is set by engineering and monitored by the mine superintendent and survey pickups. Duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check closure on the control network
steps.description: Before leaving, the surveyor closes back on a known station and compares the result with its coordinates. If the misclosure is outside tolerance, the setup is repeated.

control.basis: Site survey standard: every setup is closed on control within a stated tolerance

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common survey practice.

steps.name: Travel back to surface
steps.description: The crew packs the instruments and drives back up the ramp at the end of the run. As with the trip in, one trip covers several tasks.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the wait is the rest of the run's tasks.

steps.name: Download and reduce the observations
steps.description: In the survey office the surveyor downloads the total station, reduces the observations to mine-grid coordinates in the survey software and checks them against the field notes.

error.defect_description: Instrument or target height entered wrongly.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the as-built plans and void model
steps.description: The surveyor draws the new development or marks into the mine plans and the as-built void model, so that engineering, geology and the reserve estimate use current excavation shapes.

error.defect_description: Survey string attached to the wrong level or heading.

evidence.note: 2022 s. 14: mined voids are supplied by the Engineering Survey Department as AutoCAD solids for stopes, sills, drifts and raises.

steps.name: Check the plans and survey data
steps.description: The mine engineer looks over the updated plans and compares heading positions with the design and last month's advance, querying anything that looks off before it is used.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Correct a survey error
steps.description: The surveyor traces the error to the field notes or the reduction, corrects it and, if needed, re-shoots the point on the next run.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue the survey to supervisors and engineering
steps.description: The surveyor emails the updated plan or notes the marks on the line-up board, so the shift supervisors know the heading has line and grade and engineering has the as-built.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm the stope is empty and safe to scan
steps.description: The surveyor checks with the shift supervisor that the stope has been mucked out, the brow is barricaded and ventilation is on, and books a time when the drawpoint is free of loaders and trucks.

error.defect_description: Stope reported empty with broken ore still in it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; scans wait for the last mucking and a free drawpoint.

steps.name: Take the scanner and boom underground
steps.description: The survey crew loads the cavity monitoring scanner, its extension boom, batteries and the total station and drives down to the stope's drawpoint or top access.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Scan the empty stope with the cavity monitoring system
steps.description: Standing back from the brow, the crew pushes the scanner on its boom into the opening, positions it with the total station, and lets the laser sweep the cavity while stationary. Long or irregular stopes need scans from both the top and bottom accesses.

error.defect_description: Shadowed areas behind a pillar or bend leave gaps in the scan.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 84(2) para. 3-4 (unsafe locations identified and barricaded); no entry past the brow of an open stope

evidence.note: 2022 ss. 15 and 16.8: CMS surveys are routinely carried out and show about 1.0 m average wall overbreak. Emesent: the CMS boom-mounted scan is stationary, and newer lidar on the same boom scans a stope in 1-2 minutes, less than a third of the time. Duration including setups is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Travel back to surface with the scanner
steps.description: The crew packs the scanner and boom and drives back up the ramp, usually combining the trip with other survey tasks.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Build the stope solid and compute volumes
steps.description: The surveyor registers the point cloud to mine grid, builds a closed solid in the survey software, and compares it with the design stope to compute mined volume, overbreak and underbreak by wall, and the tonnes for the reconciliation.

error.defect_description: Solid not closed properly, so the volume is wrong.

evidence.note: 2022 s. 15: dilution and recovery are determined by comparing CMS data with stope design solids. Duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review overbreak and release the stope for backfill
steps.description: The mine engineer reviews the CMS solid against the design, notes overbreak, underbreak and ore left behind, decides whether the stope can be filled, and sends the scan to backfill planning, geology and the reconciliation.

next.condition: ore left behind or scan incomplete, rescan after more mucking

evidence.note: CMS overbreak feeds the dilution allowance used in design (s. 16.8). Rescan share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Measure monthly advance and stockpiles
steps.description: At month end the crew measures the face position of each active heading against last month's mark and picks up the outline of underground stockpiles, so engineering can report metres advanced and tonnes broken but not yet hauled.

error.defect_description: A heading measured from the wrong reference mark.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Travel back to surface after the month-end run
steps.description: The crew returns to surface once all headings on the month-end list have been measured, often over two or three days.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Compile measured advance and stockpile tonnes
steps.description: The surveyor computes metres advanced per heading and stockpile volumes, converts them to tonnes with the density factor and enters them in the month-end measurement spreadsheet for engineering and the reconciliation.

error.defect_description: Density factor or heading total keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review month-end measurements against reported advance
steps.description: The mine engineer compares surveyed metres with the metres the shift reports claimed, which also drive development bonus and contractor payment, and resolves differences before the figures go to the reconciliation and cost report.

control.basis: Contractor and bonus metres are paid on surveyed advance, not reported advance (site practice)

evidence.note: Author's estimate; development contractors (24 contractor development crew members in 2022 Table 16-10) are commonly paid on surveyed metres.

exceptions.name: Stope scan
exceptions.description: An emptied stope waits for access, is scanned with the CMS, processed into a solid and reviewed before backfill.

exceptions.name: Rescan after more mucking
exceptions.description: The scan shows ore left behind or gaps, so the stope is mucked further and scanned again.

exceptions.name: Misclosure
exceptions.description: The setup does not close on control within tolerance and is repeated.

exceptions.name: Survey error found at review
exceptions.description: The engineer finds an error in the plans and the surveyor corrects it, sometimes with a re-shoot.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the request being logged to the survey being issued
benchmarks.population: Mixed survey tasks at a small underground mine with one day-shift survey crew

evidence.note: Author's estimate: line and grade is usually given the same or next day so development is not held up; pickups and month-end work take a few days; stope scans take about a week from mucking out to release.

benchmarks.unit: metres average between hangingwall and footwall
benchmarks.population: Eagle River stopes scanned by CMS

evidence.note: Section 16.8.

benchmarks.unit: minutes per stope with a boom-mounted mobile lidar (later technology)
benchmarks.population: Vendor claim, not in use at the mine in 2019-2022

evidence.note: Vendor page; stationary CMS scans take more than three times as long.

pain_points.description: One two-person crew on day shift serves both shifts' development; when it falls behind, headings run past their line and grade or wait.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from 4 surveyors on a 14/14 rotation.

pain_points.description: Stope scans wait for the last mucking and a free drawpoint, which delays backfill and the start of the next stope.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file names survey backlog as a cause of backfill delay.

pain_points.description: Month-end measurement doubles the workload for a few days and competes with line and grade for the same crew.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Travel down a long ramp takes a large share of the crew's day, so tasks are batched into runs and individual requests wait.

evidence.note: Personnel access is by ramp (s. 16.4); travel minutes are the author's estimate.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (SRK project CAPR001445, effective 31 December 2021)
sources.publisher: SRK Consulting (Canada) Inc. for Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd.
sources.supports: Engineering Survey Department supplies mined void solids (stopes, sills, drifts, raises); ore development on vein under geology control and other development under survey control; CMS surveys routinely carried out, 1.0 m average wall overbreak, CMS compared with design solids for dilution and recovery; ramp access; 9 owner staff in mine engineering and 24 contractor development crew.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Mining Complex including the Eagle River Gold Mine, the Mishi Gold Mine and related infrastructure (Mannard and Ng)
sources.supports: Slot raise dips set by engineering and monitored by survey pickups; sill grades generally +2% with line on geology control.

sources.title: Cavity Monitoring System (CMS) Mount for Hovermap
sources.supports: CMS boom deployment of a scanner into a stope; traditional CMS is stationary, while boom-mounted mobile lidar scans a stope in 1-2 minutes, less than a third of the time.

sources.title: R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 854: Mines and Mining Plants, Occupational Health and Safety Act (e-Laws consolidation in force 1 July 2021, archived copy captured 17 January 2022)
sources.publisher: Government of Ontario (archived by the Library and Archives Canada web archive)
sources.supports: Ground examination before work begins (s. 66(1)); identification and barricading of unsafe locations (s. 84(2)).

assumptions: A case is one survey task. Travel is shared across the four to six tasks of a run, so travel steps on the main path show one task's share.
Field steps use people = 2 for the two-person survey crew.

The organisation file triggers this process only from development and mucking; month-end measurement is added as a trigger from ts-short-range-plan (mine_plan), since it is set by the monthly calendar and the plan's heading list.
Stope scans are confirmed by the shift supervisor (cms_wait), a role not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Scanning in 2019-2022 is assumed to use a stationary boom-mounted CMS laser; faster mobile lidar on the same boom is noted only as a benchmark.
Task mix, durations and queue times are the author's estimates; no published survey workload figures for this mine were found.

Hands-on time times volume implies about 6 FTE at 130 hours a month against 4.4 stated. Surveyors on a 14/14 rotation with 12-hour shifts work about 180 hours a month, so the four surveyors supply about 5.5 FTE at the validator's 130 hours; the crew runs close to full, which matches the survey backlog the organisation file describes.
